name: Stratified exemplars across the full activation range
shows: Example inputs sampled from several activation quantiles (top 0.01%, top 1%, 90th, 50th, near-zero, most negative), plus random dataset samples, each labeled with its activation value and percentile.
guards_against: Reading the unit only from its top-k extremes. Missing that moderate activations, which carry most of the mass, track a different or broader property. Not seeing whether the top-k concept is graded or a threshold effect. Confusing a rare spike with the unit's typical behavior.
image: Run the network over a large held-out set and record the unit's spatially max-pooled (and mean-pooled) activation per image. Bin by quantile and sample 8-16 images per bin. Show crops around the argmax location alongside full images.
text: Run the model over a large, diverse corpus and record the unit's activation at every token (an MLP neuron post-nonlinearity, or an SAE latent). Sample contexts by per-token activation quantile, showing about 32 tokens before the token and a few after.

name: Localized activation maps on each exemplar
shows: Where within each input the unit fires: a spatial heatmap overlaid on the image, or per-token activation coloring across the whole context, not just the max token.
guards_against: Attributing the activation to the salient object or overall topic when the unit actually responds to a background patch, an edge, a border artifact, a specific subword, punctuation, or the token after the concept. Also catches position or padding artifacts.
image: Upsample the unit's spatial activation map (feature map channel) to input resolution and overlay it. Mark the theoretical and effective receptive field of the argmax location. Shallow layers get tight crops; deep layers get full context.
text: Color every token in the shown context by activation, normalized to the unit's max over the dataset. Mark the max token, and note the absolute position index to expose position-driven units.

name: Precomputed counterfactual edits (occlusion / ablation of input parts)
shows: How the activation changes when parts of high-activating inputs are removed or altered. Results appear as a sensitivity map plus a small table of edit to activation delta.
guards_against: Correlational confounds, where the observer names a co-occurring concept instead of the causal input feature (e.g. 'dog' vs. 'grass texture'; 'legal topic' vs. the token 'Section'). Also distinguishes local from contextual dependence.
image: Sliding-window occlusion with gray or blurred patches at several scales. Also run fixed automated edits: grayscale, hue shift, blur, high-pass, horizontal flip, rotation, crop to the receptive field only, and paste the receptive-field crop onto random backgrounds. Report the activation ratio for each.
text: Leave-one-token-out deletion or masking for each preceding token in the window (or integrated gradients to the unit). Also run automated edits: truncate context to the last n tokens (n = 1, 2, 4, 8, 16), replace the max token with frequency-matched random tokens, shuffle earlier context, and change case or whitespace. Report the activation for each.

name: Low-level / surface-property correlation report
shows: How much activation variance is explained by simple, cheap-to-compute properties, regressed against activation over the dataset, with R² values and the top correlated properties.
guards_against: Over-interpreting a low-level or positional feature as a high-level semantic one, which is especially common for shallow units and for 'concept' units that are really color, frequency, or token-identity detectors. Calibrates the observer for layer depth.
image: Per receptive-field patch: mean color in several color spaces, luminance, contrast, dominant orientation (Gabor energy), spatial frequency spectrum, edge density, and spatial position. Report the R² of a small regression or gradient-boosted model and the top factors.
text: Per token: the current token's identity (how much activation variance token identity alone explains), previous token identity, position, token frequency, character class (digit, punctuation, whitespace, capitalization), and a document-level language or format label. Report R² for each, and list the top tokens by mean activation together with their counts.

name: Near-miss contrast sets
shows: Pairs or groups of inputs that look similar to the top exemplars (nearest neighbors in a reference embedding space, or same class or same token) but have low activation, shown side by side with high-activating ones.
guards_against: Overly broad labels: naming a category when the unit fires only for a subset, a viewpoint, a context, or a particular sense of a word. Contrasts force the observer to find the discriminating property.
image: For each top exemplar, retrieve the nearest neighbors in a separate model's embedding space (e.g. CLIP or penultimate layer) or same-label images, and show those with low unit activation. Also show the lowest-activating images of the top exemplars' dominant class.
text: For the tokens that most often carry the max activation, show other occurrences of the same token with low activation. Also show nearest-neighbor contexts by sentence embedding with low activation. This exposes context or word-sense conditions.

name: Activation distribution and base-rate statistics
shows: A histogram of activations (log scale) over the dataset, firing frequency above thresholds, sparsity, max and mean, the fraction of inputs with nonzero activation, and how often the proposed top concept occurs in the dataset overall.
guards_against: Mistaking a dense, broadly active unit for a selective detector. Overclaiming specificity from a handful of examples. Ignoring that a 'concept' is common enough to appear in top examples by chance. Helps the observer judge whether to give a precise or vague reading.
image: Compute the histogram over max-pooled and mean-pooled per-image activations. Report the fraction of images above 10%, 50%, and 90% of max. Give the per-class mean activation distribution (entropy over classes).
text: Compute the histogram over per-token activations. Give density (fraction of tokens active), activations per document, entropy over the token-identity distribution of firing positions, and the comparison of top-activating contexts' token frequencies to corpus base rates.

name: Output-side / downstream effect summary
shows: What the unit does to the model's computation: which outputs it promotes or suppresses directly and via ablation, as ranked lists with effect sizes.
guards_against: Purely input-side readings that miss the unit's functional role. This matters for deep units and for output-oriented units in language models, which fire on diverse inputs but consistently push one prediction, and which look incoherent from inputs alone.
image: Zero-ablate or mean-ablate the channel and report the change in class logits and accuracy, averaged over images where the unit is active. Report which classes are most helped or hurt. Optionally report the top downstream channels by weight × activation.
text: Project the neuron's output weights through the unembedding (direct logit attribution) and list the top promoted and suppressed tokens. Also report the mean-ablation effect on next-token loss and on the specific tokens predicted at its high-activation positions.

name: Clustered exemplar modes (polysemanticity view)
shows: Top-activating exemplars grouped into clusters, with the size and activation share of each cluster, so distinct modes are presented separately rather than interleaved.
guards_against: Forcing a single unifying label onto a polysemantic unit. Letting the largest mode hide minority modes. Inventing a strained abstract concept to cover unrelated clusters.
image: Embed the top ~500 receptive-field crops with an external vision model and cluster them (k chosen by silhouette score or similar). Show 6-9 exemplars per cluster with the cluster's mean activation and frequency.
text: Embed the top ~500 contexts, windowed around the max token, with a sentence encoder plus the max token's identity, and cluster them. Show several exemplars per cluster with the cluster's mean activation, frequency, and dominant tokens.
